newsitem.title: USA: US T-bond up full point, spurred by short-covering.
newsitem.headline: US T-bond up full point, spurred by short-covering.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bonds climbed to session highs in late afternoon trade, with the benchmark 30-year bond extending its rise to more than a point, spurred by short-covering and a strong futures close, market participants said.

"It's short-covering because the market didn't go down," said one long bond trader. "A lot of people interpreted the numbers as being better (for the market) than expected," he said, referring to the December Producer Price Index (PPI) and the latest weekly figures on new jobless claims released this morning.
The March T-bond contract closed near its session high as short-covering emerged in the futures pit as well, analysts at MMS International noted.
"If the market had continued to go down, people would have been happy to stay with their shorts," a trader said. "But people ran for cover because the market was going up."
Participants were also eager to square positions before the December employment report on Friday.
"Estimates on payroll growth are kind of all over the place," said the long bond trader. "The consensus seems to be in the 175,000 to 200,000 (new jobs) area."
